correctness.rationale: The four-time cumulant equals (m4-m2^2)exp(-alpha span)-2m2^2 exp(-alpha(span+middle gap)), then integrates to two positive kernels I,J. A monotone likelihood ratio in the span distribution forces J/I to decrease strictly from 1 to 1/2. Isotropic fourth-moment reduction and independent Brownian Gaussianity give the exact sign rule; the boundary t^-2 coefficient follows from I(s)=s-3+o(1), J(s)=s/2-5/4+o(1). The standalone independent moment ODE and quadrature program passed 395 deterministic checks.

originality.rationale: The velocity process itself is present in Mori et al. (2020); the claim is not its invention. Their reported exact universal observables are survival/record/maximum statistics, not fourth-cumulant sign classification. Fixed-speed arbitrary-angle RTP in Britton et al. (2026), continuous-speed OU ABP in Shee--Chaudhuri (2021), and three-phase one-dimensional switching in Santra et al. (2024) have different claimed conclusions or dynamics. The strictly decreasing critical speed-moment ratio and uniqueness across all times were not located in the searched full primary texts and relevant indices; priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: A physically natural speed-polydisperse active motion model has a complete universal classification of the sign of non-Gaussian displacement fluctuations. The sharp 4/3 and 2 thresholds and monotone one-crossing result distinguish regimes without requiring a full speed distribution, reveal a stop/go design criterion and an exact faster boundary decay, and are motivated by the established competition of speed and directional fluctuations.
